notes: All authoritative task criteria (TC1-TC6) are mutually consistent: they specify a single, coherent transformation (lowercase, collapse non-ASCII-alnum runs to one hyphen, strip edge hyphens, empty result when no ASCII alnum, TypeError on non-str) that does not contradict the existing tests in tests/test_basic.py. The current implementation in slugkit/core.py simply fails to implement the full specification, but the specification itself contains no internal contradictions or conflicts with frozen code.
rule: a conflict is demonstrated only when it names existing criteria and its witness program, run on the unmodified repository in a disposable sandbox branch, prints a line starting with 'CONTRADICTION' that names at least one of them and exits with code 3; it is GROUNDED, and may end the run as infeasible, only when every named requirement is an authoritative task criterion (TC) and the witness conforms to the constrained witness language attest-witness/1 (a positive grammar: literal inputs, allowed built-ins and standard-library functions, and functions or classes the frozen repository defines, every call origin resolved statically; enforced mechanically here and again by attest check); a demonstrated conflict that involves a derived criterion (AC) or a witness outside the language is held for a human; a claimed-only conflict never ends a run; whether the witness's inputs and comparison demonstrate that the criteria cannot all hold is the model's reasoning, recorded with its execution, not a formal proof of impossibility
input_domain: the input domain of a witness is the set of values the task names or implies: literals of the built-in types the task's statement and criteria use (plain str, int, list, dict, bytes, None and so on) and values computed from them by the unchanged repository code; instances of subclasses of built-in types, objects with overridden special methods and other adversarial values are OUTSIDE the domain unless the task names them explicitly
